name: manual_d58f0f
claim: A test that enters fastapi_app.app's real module-level singletons (registry/tracker/lifespan) from a SECOND test file/module can leave state dirty that other files' module-scoped TestClient fixtures depend on -- mocking the individual known side effects (resolve_routing_state, sync_ecc_tools, registry.route_task) is NOT sufficient to fully isolate it; the leak persisted through all of them

decisions.notes: A regression test for the CancelledError leak fix (orchestrator/fastapi_app.py, PT PR #362) called TestClient(fastapi_app.app) from tests/test_cost_guard.py. Whenever it ran in the same pytest session before tests/test_orama_integration.py, that file's routing tests started selecting 'bigmodel' instead of the expected 'ultrathink' backend -- reproduced consistently across 4 different attempts: (1) a bare  call outside any TestClient/lifespan context at all, (2) TestClient(app) with zero extra mocks, (3) TestClient(app) + mocking resolve_routing_state to match test_orama_integration.py's own client fixture exactly, (4) attempt 3 + also mocking sync_ecc_tools (a real git pull was observed running unmocked in one repro -- '[ECC Sync] Pulling latest ECC Tools...' in captured output). All 4 attempts still corrupted the other file's assertions. Notably, attempt 1 leaked WITHOUT ever touching TestClient/lifespan at all, ruling out lifespan-triggered background tasks as the sole cause -- the actual mechanism was never conclusively identified. Cut losses after ~40 minutes of bisection rather than continue burning budget; removed the test, kept the already-interactively-verified production fix, documented the gap in a code comment. NEXT TIME: don't repeat the same mocking-more-things approach -- it's already proven insufficient. A genuinely different strategy is needed, e.g. (a) run the reservation/cancellation logic through a hand-built minimal Starlette app instead of the real fastapi_app.app singleton, so no shared module state is touched at all, or (b) use pytest-xdist/subprocess isolation (run this one test in its own process) instead of trying to make it coexist cleanly with the shared-singleton suite, or (c) actually instrument what state differs before/after (diff sys.modules, registry.__dict__, tracker.__dict__, os.environ) rather than guessing at mocks one at a time.
